#====================================================================================================
# START - Testing Protocol - DO NOT EDIT OR REMOVE THIS SECTION
#====================================================================================================

# THIS SECTION CONTAINS CRITICAL TESTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR BOTH AGENTS
# BOTH MAIN_AGENT AND TESTING_AGENT MUST PRESERVE THIS ENTIRE BLOCK

# Communication Protocol:
# If the `testing_agent` is available, main agent should delegate all testing tasks to it.
#
# You have access to a file called `test_result.md`. This file contains the complete testing state
# and history, and is the primary means of communication between main and the testing agent.
#
# Main and testing agents must follow this exact format to maintain testing data. 
# The testing data must be entered in yaml format Below is the data structure:
# 
## user_problem_statement: {problem_statement}
## backend:
##   - task: "Task name"
##     implemented: true
##     working: true  # or false or "NA"
##     file: "file_path.py"
##     stuck_count: 0
##     priority: "high"  # or "medium" or "low"
##     needs_retesting: false
##     status_history:
##         -working: true  # or false or "NA"
##         -agent: "main"  # or "testing" or "user"
##         -comment: "Detailed comment about status"
##
## frontend:
##   - task: "Task name"
##     implemented: true
##     working: true  # or false or "NA"
##     file: "file_path.js"
##     stuck_count: 0
##     priority: "high"  # or "medium" or "low"
##     needs_retesting: false
##     status_history:
##         -working: true  # or false or "NA"
##         -agent: "main"  # or "testing" or "user"
##         -comment: "Detailed comment about status"
##
## metadata:
##   created_by: "main_agent"
##   version: "1.0"
##   test_sequence: 0
##   run_ui: false
##
## test_plan:
##   current_focus:
##     - "Task name 1"
##     - "Task name 2"
##   stuck_tasks:
##     - "Task name with persistent issues"
##   test_all: false
##   test_priority: "high_first"  # or "sequential" or "stuck_first"
##
## agent_communication:
##     -agent: "main"  # or "testing" or "user"
##     -message: "Communication message between agents"

# Protocol Guidelines for Main agent
#
# 1. Update Test Result File Before Testing:
#    - Main agent must always update the `test_result.md` file before calling the testing agent
#    - Add implementation details to the status_history
#    - Set `needs_retesting` to true for tasks that need testing
#    - Update the `test_plan` section to guide testing priorities
#    - Add a message to `agent_communication` explaining what you've done
#
# 2. Incorporate User Feedback:
#    - When a user provides feedback that something is or isn't working, add this information to the relevant task's status_history
#    - Update the working status based on user feedback
#    - If a user reports an issue with a task that was marked as working, increment the stuck_count
#    - Whenever user reports issue in the app, if we have testing agent and task_result.md file so find the appropriate task for that and append in status_history of that task to contain the user concern and problem as well 
#
# 3. Track Stuck Tasks:
#    - Monitor which tasks have high stuck_count values or where you are fixing same issue again and again, analyze that when you read task_result.md
#    - For persistent issues, use websearch tool to find solutions
#    - Pay special attention to tasks in the stuck_tasks list
#    - When you fix an issue with a stuck task, don't reset the stuck_count until the testing agent confirms it's working
#
# 4. Provide Context to Testing Agent:
#    - When calling the testing agent, provide clear instructions about:
#      - Which tasks need testing (reference the test_plan)
#      - Any authentication details or configuration needed
#      - Specific test scenarios to focus on
#      - Any known issues or edge cases to verify
#
# 5. Call the testing agent with specific instructions referring to test_result.md
#
# IMPORTANT: Main agent must ALWAYS update test_result.md BEFORE calling the testing agent, as it relies on this file to understand what to test next.

#====================================================================================================
# END - Testing Protocol - DO NOT EDIT OR REMOVE THIS SECTION
#====================================================================================================

Fix: AuthContext.refresh() now retries the silent admin login up to 6 times with backoff (1s,2s,3s,4s,5s) before giving up, while ProtectedRoute keeps showing the loading spinner (user===null) during retries. agent_communication:
    -agent: "main"
    -message: "USER-REPORTED BUG: 'Save shows error most of the time; I should not have to type the meeting date every time; data must not be gone on error; add 10-second auto-save.' ROOT CAUSE: frontend blocked on the meeting_date validation toast whenever the user hadn't picked one. FIX (frontend only, DataEntry.js): (1) submit() auto-fills meeting_date=today if empty (toast informs the user) instead of blocking; (2) every form change persists to localStorage under collectiq:dataentry:v2:<editId||new> (500 ms debounce); restored automatically on mount/refresh/failed save; cleared only after successful backend save; (3) 10-second idle backend auto-save (opt-out toggle in header) POSTs the first time, then PUTs subsequent auto-saves against the same id (tracked in autoCreatedId + URL replaceState) — cannot create duplicate meetings; skips when no rep has entered aging/collection numbers yet; (4) header shows live 'Saving… / Saved 12s ago / Draft saved locally 3s ago / Server save failed — draft kept locally'; (5) manual save error toast now says 'your data is safe (auto-saved locally)'. Backend unchanged. Please verify backend flow with admin@company.com/Admin@123: (a) POST /api/meetings with meeting_date='2099-12-01', title='Auto-Save Test', 1 rep named 'AutoSaveRep' with aging {d90:{mbs:1000,mcorp:500}, d60:{mbs:800,mcorp:400}, d30:{mbs:600,mcorp:300}, d15:{mbs:0,mcorp:200}, othera:{mbs:100,mcorp:50}}, weekly_collection {mbs:100,mcorp:50}, last_week_target=1000, working_days=6, branches:[{name:'Direct Sale'}], marketing_reps:[] — must return 200 with a fresh id; save it as id1. (b) PUT /api/meetings/{id1} THREE consecutive times, each modifying the rep's weekly_collection.mbs by +100 (110, 210, 310) — each must return 200. After the last PUT, the doc's rep.weekly_collection.mbs must be 310 (last-write-wins semantics). (c) GET /api/meetings — total count MUST equal (count_before + 1). Filter for meeting_date='2099-12-01' — MUST return exactly 1 doc (no duplicates from the sequential PUTs). (d) DELETE /api/meetings/{id1} → 200. Subsequent GET /api/meetings/{id1} must 404. (e) Final GET /api/meetings count must equal count_before (sanity). No 500/502 errors during the run. Do NOT test AI extraction. Do NOT touch any existing seeded meetings. Report PASS/FAIL for each step with observed values."

    -agent: "main"
    -message: "NEW ENHANCEMENT (frontend only). Data Entry page now (1) shows a week-over-week comparison chip next to each aging bucket total (90/60/30/15/Other and the 'All Buckets' sum) using the SAME rep's data from the most recent PRIOR meeting; rising outstanding = red ▲, falling = green ▼. (2) On a NEW meeting, each rep's Last Week Target field is auto-populated from that same rep's New Target (d90+d60+d30+d15) in the prior meeting, so users no longer need to type it every week. On EDIT the persisted value is preserved (never overwritten); a helper text still shows the historical prior-week New Target for reference. Implementation lives entirely in frontend/src/pages/DataEntry.js — uses getMeetings() and useMemo to find the previous meeting; useEffect handles the one-time auto-fill. Backend unchanged. Please verify multi-meeting backend flow so the frontend can rely on it: auth admin@company.com/Admin@123. (a) POST /api/meetings with meeting_date='2099-11-15', 5 reps (names 'AlphaRep','BetaRep','GammaRep','DeltaRep','EpsilonRep'), each with aging incl d15 (positive values), weekly_collection {mbs, mcorp}, last_week_target=0, working_days=6 — must return 200 and summary.last_week_target_total=0. (b) POST another meeting with meeting_date='2099-11-22', SAME 5 rep names, different aging + weekly_collection, last_week_target=100000 each — must return 200 and summary.last_week_target_total=500000. (c) GET /api/meetings — both new meetings must appear, sorted by meeting_date (ascending). (d) GET /api/meetings/{2nd_id} — every rep's stored last_week_target must be exactly 100000 (backend does NOT auto-derive; the frontend auto-filled value was sent as an explicit field). (e) GET /api/analytics/trends — the new weekly points must include coll_pct, last_week_target_total, and new_target_total for both meetings. (f) DELETE both new meetings and confirm subsequent GETs return 404. Do NOT touch existing meetings 2026-07-15 (id=1f316aec-ef04-40b4-a89a-633c51211ce5) or 2026-07-21. Report PASS/FAIL for each step with observed values."

    -agent: "main"
    -message: "USER-REPORTED BUG: 'When I edit an existing meeting and make further entry and save, it is NOT saving.' ROOT CAUSE: frontend/src/pages/DataEntry.js submit() had `if (form.reps.some((r) => !r.name.trim())) return;` — any single empty-name rep blocked the entire save. But clicking 'Add Rep' inserts a rep with name=''. So the classic user flow (open edit → click Add Rep → click Save without naming it) failed silently (toast lasted 3s, easy to miss). FIX (frontend only): submit() now silently drops empty-name reps to match how branches/marketing_reps have always been filtered. Only blocks with a 6s toast when ZERO reps have names. Also lengthened onError toast to 8s and added a console.error for the missed toasts. Backend PUT unchanged. Please verify the backend PUT flow with admin@company.com / Admin@123: (1) POST /api/auth/login. (2) GET /api/meetings — pick the ONE meeting present (id=1f316aec-ef04-40b4-a89a-633c51211ce5, meeting_date=2026-07-15). (3) PUT /api/meetings/{id} with the full existing body PLUS one extra rep (name='PlaywrightRep', full aging incl d15, weekly_collection {mbs:100,mcorp:50}, last_week_target=1000, working_days=6) — expect HTTP 200; response.reps len must be original+1 and summary.coll_pct must recompute correctly (= collected * 100 / sum(last_week_target)). (4) GET /api/meetings/{id} — new rep must be present. (5) PUT again omitting the extra rep — must return 200 and drop it from the doc. (6) Final GET count of reps must equal original count. (7) Edge case: PUT with a rep whose last_week_target=0 — coll_pct must be handled (0 or normal) with no 500. (8) Edge case: PUT with branches:[] and marketing_reps:[] — must return 200 with no schema error. (9) GET /api/analytics/trends after step 4 must return 200. No changes to /api/backup, /api/restore. Do not test AI extraction. Do not modify meetings other than the one seeded id above. Report PASS/FAIL for each step."

    -message: "BUG FIX (Cloudflare 502 while adding + backup verification). Root cause: fpdf2, openpyxl, google-genai and pandas are declared in backend/requirements.txt but were NOT installed in this pod, so any request that hit backend/export_report.py (via GET /api/meetings/{id}/export.pdf or .xlsx) crashed with ModuleNotFoundError, which the ingress/Cloudflare surfaced as a 502. Fixed by pip-installing all four packages and restarting the backend. Please run a smoke test using admin@company.com / Admin@123 (cookie via POST /api/auth/login): (1) POST /api/meetings — full-shape body with 1 rep (all aging buckets, weekly_collection, last_week_target=1000, working_days=6), 1 branch named 'Direct Sale', quotation, 1 marketing_rep — must return 200; response.summary.coll_pct must equal round(collected*100/last_week_target_total, 2). (2) GET /api/meetings/{new_id}/export.pdf — must return 200 with Content-Type starting with 'application/pdf'. (3) GET /api/meetings/{new_id}/export.xlsx — must return 200 with an XLSX content-type (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet). (4) GET /api/backup — must return 200 with app='CollectIQ', a settings dict, and meetings array whose length equals GET /api/meetings length; the meeting created in step 1 must be present. (5) POST /api/restore with the EXACT backup from step 4 — must return {ok:true, restored_meetings:<same count>} and subsequent GET /api/meetings must still return the same count. (6) POST /api/restore with {app:'NotCollectIQ'} — must return 400 and NOT wipe data. (7) DELETE /api/meetings/{new_id} — must return 200 and subsequent GET must 404. Do not test AI extraction (no key needed for this test)."

    -message: "COLLECTION % FORMULA CHANGE. Per user, Collection % is now (MBS+MCORP collected) ÷ last_week_target — replacing the old 'collected ÷ new_target'. Please verify with admin@company.com / Admin@123 (cookie login POST /api/auth/login): (1) GET /api/meetings — for each meeting: sum of reps[].last_week_target equals summary.last_week_target_total; summary.coll_pct equals round(summary.collected * 100 / summary.last_week_target_total, 2) when last_week_target_total > 0; is 0 when the sum is 0. (2) GET /api/analytics/trends — each weekly point's coll_pct follows the same rule. (3) GET /api/reps/Arun/history — each point's coll_pct equals round(collected * 100 / that meeting's Arun.last_week_target, 2) (0 when last_week_target is 0). (4) POST /api/meetings then GET — set two reps with known last_week_target and weekly_collection and confirm the coll_pct matches the expected ratio (then DELETE for cleanup). No changes to /api/backup or /api/restore. Do not test AI extraction."
